name: Sweephilt Review
description: Close two fingers around the ricasso and three around the grip so the point answers every small turn of the wrist.

name: Hooding Counterpoise
description: Stand side-on with the blade level at the hip so the body offers the foe the smallest possible line.

name: Gnawing Stoccata
description: Throw the front foot forward and extend the arm until the point lands at the centre of the chest.

name: Backward Whipblade
description: After the thrust push off the front heel and draw the rear leg under the body to regain guard.

name: Slimtang Cowl
description: Turn the forte inward to knock a thrust off the inner line without moving the feet.

name: Hard Needlepoint
description: Keep the point steady at the height of the foe's eyes so he hesitates to step inside your reach.

name: Calm Cupedge
description: Extend the arm toward a marker and step forward until the point just touches it to learn your own reach.

name: Pashit
description: Lunge from guard to full extension and hold one count before returning so balance at the end of the thrust is learned.

name: Sweptdodge
description: Drive the front heel into the ground to snap the body back into guard right after a thrust.

name: Ready Cuphilt
description: Drop the point low and sweep it across the body to turn aside a thrust aimed at the belly.

name: Measured Pasguard
description: Repeat guard then lunge then recovery to a steady count until each phase takes the same time.

name: Tipwhip Count
description: Hold the point still before a hanging flame without stirring it so the wrist learns calm.

name: Sweptreview
description: Roll the thumb along the ricasso to turn the point a finger's width without moving the forearm.

name: Square Bellguard
description: Send the point straight at the hollow of the throat with a short quick extension of the arm.

name: Quick Passata
description: Slip the point under the foe's raised arm and drive it into the ribs on his open side.

name: Pasguard Wedge
description: Make a small circle with the point to wind a thrust off its line and past your shoulder.

name: Foildash
description: Flick the point sharply onto the foe's leading hand to loosen his grip on his own weapon.

name: Folded Whipblade
description: Draw the arm back along the line of the thrust so the foe cannot seize or beat the blade.

name: Pascowl
description: Hold the point low and to the outside so the blade covers the knee and the hip.

name: Planted Tipwhip
description: Raise the hilt to the shoulder and cant the blade inward to close the upper inner line.

name: Ready Bellguard
description: Extend the blade across the outer line with the point forward to bar a thrust from that side.

name: Ready Sweephilt
description: Roll the blade over the lead shoulder to sweep a high thrust out to the open side.

name: Sweptcowl
description: Catch a glancing blade in the cup of the hilt and twist it away from your hand.

name: Quiet Fleche
description: Shift from one guard to the next with a half step so the foe cannot predict the open line.

name: Steady Counterpoise
description: Look along the blade to confirm that the point and the foe's eye form one straight line.

name: Folded Slimtang
description: Snap the blade down across the forearm to stop a rising thrust the moment it starts.

name: Light Stoccata
description: Slide the front foot a hand's breadth forward and bring the rear foot after it without crossing the legs.

name: Nimble Passata
description: Step the rear foot back and then the front foot to open the gap by two short paces.

name: Backward Volte
description: Cross the rear foot over the front and plant it ahead to close a long gap in one pass.

name: Stepping Remise
description: Step wide to the weapon side so the foe's straight thrust meets only empty air.

name: Wide Remise
description: Keep the hips low and level through the lunge so the point arrives with the weight behind it.

name: Sweptgauge
description: Rest the weight on the balls of the feet and feel the ground for the foe's coming step.

name: Cupedge Bump
description: Extend the arm fully before the foot lands so the point arrives ahead of the body.

name: Cuphilt Gauge
description: Raise the unarmed hand behind you as a counterweight and keep the shoulders level through every lunge.

name: Open Needlepoint
description: Hold the point toward the foe's face and give ground only when he presses past it.

name: Sweptwedge
description: Turn the wrist a little to move a thrust aside rather than swinging the whole arm.

name: Shifting Cupedge
description: Push from the rear heel on every advance so the front leg stays free to place the foot.

name: Foilgauge
description: Let a thin thread of qi run to the point and hold it there to sharpen every small motion.

name: Pasdash
description: Release the held qi into the front leg as you lunge so the thrust lands before the foe can react.

name: Holding Counterpoise
description: Brush the foe's blade with the point and a pulse of qi to move it just wide of your body.

name: Stepping Lunge
description: Pull the qi back up the arm as you recoil so the recovery is as quick as the thrust.

name: Lunge Cowl
description: Flick the point toward one eye and draw it back at once so the foe flinches into the wrong guard.

name: Flechebump
description: Tap the foe's wrist with the quickened point to numb the hand for a breath.

name: Settled Cuphilt
description: Hold one breath and a thin film of qi along the blade to cover the line while the foe probes.

name: Measured Bellguard
description: Wrap the first two fingers over the ricasso and feed a little qi into them for finer point control.

name: Solid Needlepoint
description: Tilt the cup of the hilt up to catch a thrust and let qi in the wrist lock the blade aside.

name: Sweptstrike
description: Press the thumb down on the grip as you lunge to pin the point onto its line.

name: Foilstay
description: Spring the wrist upward after the thrust to return the blade to cover with no extra arm motion.

name: Straight Stoccata
description: Swing the cup of the hilt in a short hook against the jaw of a foe who has closed too near.

name: Sweptnote
description: Loosen the grip and tighten it again to feel through the hilt whether the foe's blade is pushing.

name: Holding Pasguard
description: Drop the pommel across the body to stop a low thrust at the belly line.

name: Pasreview
description: Slide the hand a finger forward on the hilt while pressed so the leverage shifts and the foe's push fails.

name: Lowered Sweephilt
description: Draw breath slowly in guard and let qi settle in the belly before any move begins.

name: Firm Fleche
description: Exhale sharply as you lunge so the qi leaves the body together with the point.

name: Snug Slimtang
description: Hold the breath for one beat and turn the blade to push a thrust away from the centre.

name: Sideways Whipblade
description: Walk backward in guard on a slow breath to calm the circulation after a hard exchange.

name: Watching Bellguard
description: Listen to the foe's breath and watch his chest swell to guess when he will thrust.

name: Remisestrike
description: Lunge on one breath and recover on the next and lunge again with no pause between them.

name: Whipblade Count
description: Fix both eyes along the blade and feel with qi where the narrow line toward the foe lies.

name: Swepthit
description: Thrust along the sighted line without letting the shoulder swing and keep the point on it to the end.

name: Remise Stay
description: Beat the foe's blade across the line to knock his point off its path for one moment.

name: Kept Pasguard
description: Lay the blade along the line toward the foe so any thrust must first pass the steel.

name: Remisetrot
description: Step off the line by a hand's breadth and bring the point back onto a new line at once.

name: Quick Lunge
description: Drop the point onto the foe's forearm from above after he extends along the line.

name: Stepping Volte
description: Retreat along the same line you advanced on so the foe's counter finds nothing but the steel.

name: Voltestrike
description: Hold the lunge until the foe commits his front foot and then thrust into the gap he leaves.

name: Level Tipwhip
description: Thrust at the first twitch of the foe's advance to stop him before his step lands.

name: Flechehop
description: Step in on the hinge of the foe's thrust at the instant his arm is fully extended.

name: Swepthusk
description: Delay the parry a beat so a late or doubled thrust is caught and turned aside.

name: Kind Sweephilt
description: Count the foe's rhythm of steps and thrusts silently until the gap in it shows.
